timeline.claim: The source established an upper OMG boundary near SPY 567.50 and a lower boundary near 565.98-566.00, with limited but identifiable room before support.
The preferred upside sequence was a close, a fade or test that held, and renewed buying pressure; no qualifying early OMG trade was reported.
The source said an aggressive chart target was touched but might have moved too quickly to produce an option fill; this was not counted as a trade.
The source reported May 16 567 puts filled at 6.44 for an intrarange scalp.
After reducing the target as price bounced, the source reported the 567 puts filled at 6.58.
The source explicitly disclosed that the presenter was trading in simulation that day.
The source reported simulated May 16 567 calls at 6.57 with a 6.70 scalp target after a double-bottom and flag discussion.
The 567 calls remained approximately even after repeated rotations and the original 6.70 target was not reported filled.
The source reported May 16 567 puts at 6.21 with a 6.41 target linked to approximately SPY 566.31.
The source reported the 567-put target filled at 6.41 after missing an earlier discretionary exit window.
The open 567 calls were bid around 5.99, about 0.58 below entry, but the source retained them based on broader bullish bias and weekly expiry.
A downside OMG close occurred; the source waited for a bounce and corrected a wrong contract selection before entry.
The source reported May 16 566 puts at 6.31 with a 6.69 target linked to approximately SPY 564.81.
The source reported the OMG puts taken out at 6.77 after considering nearby support and taking the available profit.
The source disclosed two open 567-call positions; the pick-of-the-day call was below its entry and bid near 5.25.
The source acknowledged missing a clean downside 10-MA rejection while focused on the upside positions.
Near recording end, the source identified SPY 563 as a line for taking at least half of the losing call exposure off before weekend risk.

claims.label: RANGE_SCALP_TO_NEARBY_STRUCTURE
claims.claim: The source used nearby range support and resistance to define modest put scalp targets rather than projecting a larger directional move.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Deterministic range labels, synchronized SPY bars, executable option paths, simulated order logs, spreads, and fees.

claims.label: FAILED_SCALP_BECOMES_RECOVERY_POSITION
claims.claim: A 567-call scalp targeting 0.13 was retained after the target failed and the position moved materially adverse, with the rationale shifting to weekly expiry and broader bullish recovery.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Exact simulated fills, position size, bid/ask path, MFE/MAE, time-underwater, and a mandatory failed-scalp exit baseline.

claims.label: OMG_CLOSE_BOUNCE_RENEWED_WEAKNESS
claims.claim: The downside OMG entry followed a boundary close, a small bounce, and renewed weakness rather than immediate first-touch execution.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Deterministic OMG labels, synchronized bars, executable option paths, simulated fill logs, costs, and first-touch and first-close baselines.

claims.label: LOSING_THESIS_ATTENTION_COST
claims.claim: The source acknowledged missing clean downside opportunities while monitoring and defending losing upside positions.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Timestamped candidate setups, active-position state, attention or screen-focus telemetry, fills, and opportunity-cost replay.

claims.label: LATE_PARTIAL_WEEKEND_INVALIDATION
claims.claim: A SPY 563 partial-exit line was introduced only after the calls were materially adverse and weekend event risk was under discussion.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: End-of-day simulated positions, Monday gap outcome, exact option path, full and partial stop baselines, and weekend-risk segmentation.
